subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What false accusation drives the central plot of Atonement?
options: Cecilia is accused of murder
Paul Marshall is accused of fraud
Briony wrongly accuses Robbie of raping Lola
Robbie is wrongly accused of theft
questions.explain: The thirteen-year-old Briony falsely identifies Robbie Turner as Lola's attacker, a crime he did not commit.

questions.q: A 'new historicist' reading of a literary text would most characteristically:
options: treat the text as one of many cultural documents circulating within and shaping the power relations of its period
focus only on the reader's emotional response
judge the text purely by its formal elegance and unity
read the text as a timeless expression of universal human nature
questions.explain: New historicism situates a text among the period's other discourses, reading literature and history as mutually constitutive.

questions.q: What does Briony witness at the fountain that she misinterprets early in the novel?
options: A robbery
Robbie attacking Cecilia
A drowning
Cecilia stripping to her underwear and entering the fountain after a vase breaks, which Briony reads as Robbie's coercion
questions.explain: Briony sees Cecilia undress and plunge into the fountain to retrieve a vase fragment and wrongly interprets Robbie as dominating her.

questions.q: 'Foregrounding' in stylistic analysis means:
options: placing a scene at the front of the play
describing the background setting
summarising the plot's opening
making a linguistic feature prominent through deviation or repetition so it draws attention
questions.explain: Foregrounding makes language conspicuous through patterning or deviation, directing the reader's interpretive attention.

questions.q: AO2 is best satisfied when a student:
options: describes the writer's life and times
summarises three critics' opinions
lists the events of the plot in order
analyses how specific choices of form, structure and language create meaning and effect
questions.explain: AO2 rewards close analysis of the writer's craft and the effects of formal, structural and linguistic choices.

questions.q: What does the novel suggest about the power of fiction and storytelling?
options: Fiction is harmless entertainment with no consequences
Only non-fiction has moral weight
Storytelling can both destroy lives, as Briony's tale ruins Robbie, and attempt to redeem, as her novel seeks atonement
Fiction always reveals the truth
questions.explain: Briony's imagination causes catastrophe yet also becomes her means of atonement, dramatising fiction's dual power.

questions.q: A 'post-colonial' reading is most concerned with:
options: the recurrence of a single image
representations of empire, the colonised 'other', hybridity and cultural power
metre and rhyme scheme
the purging of pity and fear in the audience
questions.explain: Post-colonial criticism interrogates how texts construct empire, the colonised subject and relations of cultural power.

questions.q: How does the unreliable narration affect the reader's trust in the story of Atonement?
options: It only affects the wartime scenes
It destabilises the narrative, since the events were shaped and changed by Briony the author
It guarantees a fully objective account
It is irrelevant to interpretation
questions.explain: Learning Briony controlled and altered the story forces the reader to question everything previously presented as fact.

questions.q: What is the central metafictional twist revealed in the novel's final section?
options: Briony is revealed as the author of the novel, who admits she altered events in her fiction
Robbie wrote the story
The whole narrative was a dream of Cecilia's
Briony was innocent all along
questions.explain: An ageing Briony discloses that she wrote the preceding narrative, making the book a self-conscious act of authorship.

questions.q: When a critic's view is quoted in an essay, the most analytically rigorous use of it is to:
options: accept it as the final, authoritative answer
quote it without further comment
place it at the start to replace the student's own argument
treat it as a position to be tested, endorsed or challenged against the text
questions.explain: Critics' views (AO5) should be deployed as debatable positions that the student evaluates through their own reading.

questions.q: A 'psychoanalytic' (Freudian) reading would typically attend to:
options: the text's fidelity to historical fact
the rhythm and metre of the verse alone
the economic base determining the cultural superstructure
the unconscious, repression, desire and symbolic expressions of inner conflict
questions.explain: Psychoanalytic criticism reads texts for unconscious drives, repression and symbolic enactments of psychic conflict.

questions.q: How does Atonement reflect its postmodern context?
options: By avoiding any reference to writing or authorship
By presenting a single objective historical record
By rejecting all narrative experimentation
Through self-conscious metafiction, an unreliable author-narrator and questioning the reliability of any story
questions.explain: The novel's foregrounding of its own constructedness and authorial control marks it as characteristically postmodern.

questions.q: 'Framing' as a structural device most often refers to:
options: the use of iambic pentameter throughout
a story enclosed within another narrative that introduces and concludes it
the alphabetical ordering of chapters
the metaphors clustered in a single stanza
questions.explain: A frame narrative encloses an inner tale, often shaping how the reader judges its reliability and meaning.

questions.q: 'Tone' in a literary text refers to:
options: the writer's or speaker's attitude towards the subject, conveyed through diction and form
the moral lesson of the work
the historical setting
the literal sound of words read aloud
questions.explain: Tone is the implied attitude or stance of the speaker towards subject or audience, signalled by linguistic choices.

questions.q: Which is the best example of using context (AO3) analytically rather than as 'bolted-on' background?
options: A paragraph narrating the author's biography before discussing the text
Showing how the poem's anxieties about industrialisation shape its imagery of the polluted river
Listing the dates of the period at the essay's start
Stating that the text was written in the nineteenth century
questions.explain: Context is used well when it illuminates specific textual choices rather than sitting as detached background.

questions.q: A 'reader-response' approach holds that meaning is:
options: produced in the interaction between the text and the reader's act of interpretation
fixed entirely by the author's stated intention
determined solely by the historical context of composition
irrelevant to literary study
questions.explain: Reader-response criticism locates meaning in the transaction between text and reader rather than in the author alone.

questions.q: What does the play Briony writes at the start, 'The Trials of Arabella', foreshadow about her character?
options: Her wish to leave the Tallis family
Her dislike of writing
Her controlling, order-seeking imagination that will later impose a false narrative on real events
Her future career as a nurse
questions.explain: Briony's childhood drama reveals an authorial urge to shape and control events that anticipates her fateful accusation.

questions.q: A response arguing that a text 'cannot be reduced to a single meaning' and surveying competing readings is engaging most strongly with:
options: AO2 only
AO4
AO1 only
AO5
questions.explain: Acknowledging multiple, competing interpretations is the core of AO5.

questions.q: When two texts are compared, a 'point of divergence' is most valuable when it:
options: reveals how each writer handles a shared concern differently, illuminating both
shows the texts are completely unrelated
repeats a similarity already noted
proves one text is superior
questions.explain: Productive comparison uses difference to sharpen understanding of each text's distinctive method and meaning.

questions.q: An 'ecocritical' reading would be most interested in:
options: the gendered power relations within the household
the text's depiction of class struggle
the relationship between the text, the non-human world and the environment
the repressed desires of the central characters
questions.explain: Ecocriticism examines how literature represents nature, place and humanity's relationship with the environment.

questions.q: What misdirected letter from Robbie does Briony read, shaping her misunderstanding?
options: A letter confessing to a crime
A blackmail demand
An obscene draft note containing a crude word, sent to Cecilia by mistake
A suicide note
questions.explain: Robbie accidentally sends an explicit version of his note to Cecilia; Briony reads it and casts him as a 'maniac'.

questions.q: Which historical military event forms the backdrop to Robbie's section in Part Two?
options: The D-Day landings
The Blitz on London
The Battle of the Somme
The retreat and evacuation at Dunkirk
questions.explain: Part Two follows Robbie through the chaotic British retreat to Dunkirk in 1940.

questions.q: 'Dramatic irony' occurs when:
options: the play breaks the fourth wall
the audience knows something a character on stage does not
a character speaks in verse while others speak in prose
the chorus comments on the action
questions.explain: Dramatic irony arises from the gap between the audience's knowledge and a character's ignorance of it.

questions.q: Who is actually responsible for the assault on Lola Quincey?
options: Robbie Turner
Paul Marshall, whom Lola later marries
Cecilia's father
Briony's brother Leon
questions.explain: The wealthy Paul Marshall is the real assailant, and Lola ultimately marries him, allowing the truth to stay buried.

questions.q: A response that explores how a text can sustain feminist, Marxist and psychoanalytic readings is primarily demonstrating which assessment objective?
options: AO3
AO5
AO2
AO4
questions.explain: AO5 rewards engagement with different interpretations, including the application of distinct critical lenses.

questions.q: In narrative theory, 'free indirect discourse' is best defined as:
options: an authorial commentary that judges the characters explicitly
a character's thoughts rendered in the third person yet inflected with that character's own idiom and feeling
direct speech reported within quotation marks
a first-person narrator addressing the reader directly
questions.explain: Free indirect discourse blends the narrator's third-person report with a character's voice, blurring the line between the two.

questions.q: How are Robbie and Cecilia's social positions relevant to Briony's accusation being believed?
options: Cecilia is a servant
Robbie is an aristocrat above suspicion
Robbie is the cleaning-lady's son, so class prejudice makes the accusation against him easier to accept
Both come from the same wealthy family
questions.explain: Robbie's lower-class origins as the charlady's son make the Tallises and authorities readier to believe him guilty.

questions.q: What painful truth does the elderly Briony confess about Robbie and Cecilia's fates?
options: They emigrated to America
They were happily reunited as shown
They forgave Briony in person
Both died in the war and never reunited; Briony gave them a happy ending only in fiction
questions.explain: Briony admits Robbie died at Dunkirk and Cecilia in the Balham Tube bombing, and that their reunion exists only in her novel.

questions.q: Which sentence best demonstrates an integrated, analytical (rather than descriptive) point?
options: The character is angry in this scene.
This passage is about anger and conflict.
The clipped monosyllables and end-stopped lines enact the speaker's controlled rage, refusing the release that fuller rhythm would allow.
Anger is a theme that appears in the text.
questions.explain: Analytical writing links a precise technique to its effect on meaning, rather than merely naming a theme.

questions.q: The most sophisticated use of a critical quotation is to:
options: agree with it uncritically
place it at the end as a flourish
engage with it dialectically, qualifying or contesting it through close textual evidence
ignore it entirely
questions.explain: AO5 rewards a critical dialogue with other readings, tested against the student's own analysis of the text.
